open_points.subject: 02_rules.md:Status
open_points.text: The owner accepted on 2026-11-18 the single principal and HTTPS rules of A5, the values of A8, the dependency policy of A9 and the absence of removal in the first version (A3).
open_points.question: Are A1, A2, A4, A6, A7, A10 and the remaining rules of A3 and A5 accepted decisions, as their headings say, or are they only prototype findings still requiring owner acceptance?
options: All sections headed Accepted decision are accepted
Only the decisions expressly listed in Status are accepted
The unlisted sections are evidence-backed but still open
open_points.default_guess: Treat every section headed Accepted decision as accepted and expand Status to say so.

witness.initial: A later agent reads both Status and the Accepted decision headings.
events: One implementer treats A7 as binding because it is headed Accepted decision.
Another treats A7 as unaccepted because Status does not list it among the owner's acceptances.
outcomes: The service is designed around one clock reading per operation.
The clock policy is changed or deferred without an owner decision.
witness.observer: The owner and later design agents

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: A scan gives each regular file of the photo folder exactly one status.
open_points.question: Does a scan recurse into ordinary subfolders, and which regular files constitute the scan when OQ-05 asked whether everything under `foto` or only a chosen part belongs to delivery?
options: Only direct children of the photo folder
All regular files recursively except ignored subtrees
A separately selected subset
open_points.default_guess: Scan recursively beneath the configured photo folder, excluding ignored names and subtrees.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: A scan gives each regular file of the photo folder exactly one status.
open_points.question: How can rule 4 classify something that “cannot be read as a regular file” if only regular files enter the status rules, and what happens when a file changes type or disappears during a scan?
options: Only files confirmed regular are reported; races are `not_ready_or_absent`
Directory entries are candidates and rule 4 rejects non-regular entries
Only regular files are candidates, but a later failed recheck uses rule 4
open_points.default_guess: Take directory entries as candidates, ignore symbolic links, and use rule 4 when a candidate cannot be safely reopened as the same regular file.

witness.initial: A directory entry is a regular file when enumeration begins and is replaced by a FIFO before it is opened.
events: The scanner applies the status rules.
outcomes: The entry is omitted because it is no longer a regular file.
The entry is reported as rejected under rule 4.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: cannot be read as a regular file
open_points.question: Which exact condition selects `not_a_regular_file`, `too_large` or `unreadable_file`, and which reason wins when more than one condition is observed?
options: Type mismatch gives `not_a_regular_file`, size/read-limit failure gives `too_large`, and open/read failure gives `unreadable_file`
Every failure to establish a readable regular file gives `unreadable_file`
The implementation may choose among the three
open_points.default_guess: Use `not_a_regular_file` for a non-regular object, `too_large` for a size over the source limit, and `unreadable_file` for permission or I/O failure.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: does not begin with a JPEG, PNG or WEBP signature
open_points.question: What exact byte signatures and minimum lengths count as JPEG, PNG and WEBP, especially for truncated or variant files?
options: Use fixed magic-byte patterns defined by policy
Use the image library's format detector
Accept any prefix commonly associated with the three formats
open_points.default_guess: Define and import a closed table of magic-byte patterns, including the required RIFF/WEBP fields.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: Syncthing's temporary and bookkeeping names
open_points.question: What exact names or patterns are ignored, with what case sensitivity, and does the rule apply to every path component?
options: A closed case-sensitive pattern set applied to every component
Whatever the installed Syncthing version currently uses
Only well-known temporary names at the scan root
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed, versioned, case-sensitive pattern set on every path component.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: same content as an earlier file of this scan, in sorted path order
open_points.question: What representation and comparison define sorted path order, and is the duplicate reason the basename or the path relative to the photo folder?
options: Unicode code-point order of normalized relative paths; return the relative path
Filesystem byte order; return the relative path
Locale-aware order; return the basename
open_points.default_guess: Sort normalized relative POSIX paths by Unicode code point and return the earlier relative path.

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: INV-01: after a placement the source file has the bytes it had before (`test_a_placed_photo_keeps_no_metadata_and_the_source_is_untouched`).
open_points.question: What must the Required tests show for the full invariant that no operation creates, changes, moves or deletes anything in a source folder, beyond checking one file's bytes after placement?
options: Check directory entries, names, bytes and metadata before and after scan, placement and marking
Narrow INV-01 to source bytes during placement
Add separate witnesses for every source-folder mutation forbidden by INV-01
open_points.default_guess: Add witnesses for scan, placement and marking that compare the complete source tree, including entries, bytes and metadata.

open_points.subject: A2
open_points.text: A stored image is a newly encoded JPEG made from the decoded pixels of the source. Transparent areas become white. The camera orientation is applied, then the longest side is reduced to the limit when it is larger.
open_points.question: Which frame, color conversion, resampling algorithm, rounding rule and alpha-compositing color space produce the stored JPEG?
options: Define a deterministic transformation recipe
Use the pinned image library's defaults
Permit any visually equivalent JPEG
open_points.default_guess: Define a deterministic backend recipe, including first-frame handling, RGB conversion, white compositing, orientation, dimensions and resampling.

open_points.subject: A2
open_points.text: A source above the pixel limit fails with `too_many_pixels`
open_points.question: How is the pixel count computed for animated or multi-frame images, and is the limit inclusive?
options: Width × height of the selected frame; reject only when greater than the limit
Sum pixels across every frame; reject at or above the limit
Reject all animated inputs
open_points.default_guess: Reject animated inputs or explicitly use the selected first frame; reject when width × height is greater than 80,000,000.

open_points.subject: A2
open_points.text: The photo moment is the camera's original time, then the camera's general time, then the file's modification time.
open_points.question: Which concrete metadata fields constitute the original and general camera times, how are conflicting duplicate fields chosen, and what happens when a field is malformed?
options: Define an ordered closed list of metadata tags and skip malformed candidates
Let the image library choose a date
Any metadata value conventionally described as original or general time is acceptable
open_points.default_guess: Define an ordered list of supported tags and skip malformed or implausible candidates before trying the next source.

open_points.subject: A2
open_points.text: the moment is not more than one day after the file's modification time
open_points.question: Does exactly 24 hours after the modification time count, and are camera and file times converted to UTC before this comparison?
options: Exactly 24 hours is accepted; compare normalized UTC instants
Exactly 24 hours is rejected
Compare their offset-free representations
open_points.default_guess: Accept a difference of exactly 24 hours and compare normalized UTC instants.

open_points.subject: A2
open_points.text: A camera time with no offset is read in the configured time zone.
open_points.question: How are ambiguous and nonexistent Europe/Madrid local times resolved at daylight-saving transitions?
options: Choose the earlier fold and reject nonexistent local times
Choose the later fold and shift nonexistent times forward
Treat either case as invalid and fall back to the next time source
open_points.default_guess: Treat ambiguous or nonexistent local camera times as invalid and fall back to the next candidate.

open_points.subject: A2
open_points.text: The publication body has `client_visible` false, no section and no caption (R0-06, OQ-05).
open_points.question: What exact values are supplied for the other M05 fields owned by the deliverer, especially `intake_id` and `intake_source`?
options: Derive them from the placement using specified formulas or constants
Have the calling flow fill them later
Leave them null or absent where the Portal permits
open_points.default_guess: Specify a deterministic `intake_id` derived from project and source identities and a named imported constant for `intake_source`.

open_points.subject: A2
open_points.text: INV-05: a published delivery is absent from the client's overview until the owner shows it (E2E, `a delivered photo stays hidden from the client`).
open_points.question: Must the witness directly assert that every publication body built by the deliverer has `client_visible` false, rather than only observing the Portal's resulting visibility?
options: Directly assert the body field and retain the E2E behavior check
Narrow INV-05 to the observed Portal behavior
Treat the Portal observation alone as sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Add a direct assertion of `client_visible == false` on every built body.

open_points.subject: A3
open_points.text: One call places from 1 to 50 photos. A malformed source id refuses the whole call before anything is written.
open_points.question: What exact refusal occurs for zero photos, more than 50 photos, a malformed project id, or duplicate source ids in the same call, and which validation wins when several are present?
options: Reject the whole request with specified request-level codes before lookup or writes
Deduplicate repeated source ids and process the rest
Report each invalid item independently except malformed source ids
open_points.default_guess: Validate authentication, project id, connection, request cardinality and every source id before writes, with a specified precedence and request-level error codes.

open_points.subject: A3
open_points.text: A source that is not `ready` and has no placement fails with `not_ready_or_absent`. A source whose content changed after the scan fails with `source_changed`.
open_points.question: When the path is absent, settling, rejected, replaced, or now duplicates another file, what evidence distinguishes `source_changed` from `not_ready_or_absent`, and which result wins?
options: A requested source id is tied to a scan token or path snapshot, allowing a change check
Any missing current content is `not_ready_or_absent`; only a known path with different bytes is `source_changed`
Any failure to find the requested hash at the prior path is `source_changed`
open_points.default_guess: Bind each source id to the relative path observed by the scan; a different hash at that path is `source_changed`, while absence or a non-ready unchanged file is `not_ready_or_absent`.

open_points.subject: A3
open_points.text: A failure of one photo is reported in its item and the others proceed.
open_points.question: In what order are items processed, may later items observe writes made by earlier items in the same call, and what happens to remaining items after a process-level storage failure?
options: Process in request order with independent item transactions
Process in arbitrary order with equivalent outcomes
Use one transaction for records while reporting item failures
open_points.default_guess: Process in request order with one isolated transaction per item, stopping only on an unrecoverable service failure.

open_points.subject: A3
open_points.text: INV-06: a second placement returns the first publication and leaves the stored file's modification time unchanged (`test_placing_again_returns_the_same_result_without_writing`).
open_points.question: What must show that a repeated placement writes nothing at all and that at most one placement record exists, rather than merely leaving the image modification time unchanged?
options: Assert record count, record bytes, image bytes and metadata, and absence of all write calls
Narrow the invariant to the stored image
Rely on unchanged modification time as a proxy for every write
open_points.default_guess: Add assertions for a single placement record and zero backend writes on replay.

open_points.subject: A4
open_points.text: A mark needs an existing placement of the same project, otherwise it is refused with `not_placed`.
open_points.question: What result is returned when the project is unknown or unconfirmed, an existing mark also exists, or the source id is malformed, and in what order are these checks performed?
options: Authentication and syntax, then connection, placement, existing mark and conflict
Existing mark replay/conflict before connection and placement checks
Every failed condition maps to `not_placed`
open_points.default_guess: Use authentication, syntax, confirmed-connection, placement, then replay/conflict precedence.

open_points.subject: A4
open_points.text: The same `photo_id` again answers `replayed` with the first mark.
open_points.question: Does a replayed marking operation still read the service clock once under A7 even though it must preserve the first `marked_at` and write nothing?
options: Every operation reads once, including replay and refusal
Only operations that need a fresh instant read the clock
Replay reads the clock but discards the value
open_points.default_guess: Only an operation that may create a fresh mark reads the clock, once, after validation and before the write.

witness.initial: A placement already has a mark and the caller repeats the same `photo_id`.
events: The mark endpoint authenticates and finds the existing mark.
outcomes: The clock is read once because A7 says each operation reads it once.
The clock is not read because replay returns the stored mark and writes no fresh timestamp.
witness.observer: A deterministic test clock and telemetry

open_points.subject: A5
open_points.text: Any other value is refused before the request is handled.
open_points.question: What HTTP status, response body and application error are returned for a missing, malformed or wrong token, and does “before the request is handled” precede request parsing and project lookup?
options: A single indistinguishable 401 response before body parsing
Different responses for missing, malformed and wrong tokens
Framework-default authentication errors
open_points.default_guess: Return one indistinguishable 401 response before body parsing or project lookup.

open_points.subject: A5
open_points.text: The token is 256 bits from a cryptographic random source, kept in a file only its owner can read. The service does not start when the file is readable by others or the token has fewer than 32 characters.
open_points.question: Must startup verify an encoding that represents exactly 256 random bits, or is any owner-only string of at least 32 characters accepted despite the first sentence?
options: Require a specified encoding of exactly 32 random bytes
Accept any string of at least 32 characters
Require at least 256 bits of measured entropy
open_points.default_guess: Require a canonical encoding of exactly 32 random bytes and reject whitespace or malformed encodings.

witness.initial: The token file is owner-only and contains 32 repeated `a` characters.
events: The service starts and loads the file.
outcomes: Startup rejects it because it is not a 256-bit cryptographically generated token.
Startup accepts it because it has at least 32 characters and correct permissions.

open_points.subject: A5
open_points.text: kept in a file only its owner can read
open_points.question: Which owner and permission checks are required, including group/other write access, ACLs, symbolic links and parent-directory access?
options: Require an expected service owner, regular non-symlink file and no group/other permissions or ACL access
Check only group/other read bits
Trust deployment tooling to enforce ownership
open_points.default_guess: Require a regular non-symlink file owned by the service account with mode 0600 and no broader ACL access.

open_points.subject: A5
open_points.text: Outside the loopback interface the service is reached only over HTTPS (OQ-07).
open_points.question: Does the service terminate TLS itself or trust a reverse proxy, how is the original scheme authenticated, and which IPv4/IPv6 addresses count as loopback?
options: The service terminates TLS on every non-loopback listener
A trusted reverse proxy terminates TLS and the service validates trusted forwarding data
Deployment networking alone guarantees the rule
open_points.default_guess: Use a trusted reverse proxy and bind the service itself to loopback or a private socket, with no direct external HTTP listener.

open_points.subject: A5
open_points.text: An operation on a project with no connection is refused with `unknown_project`, and one with an unconfirmed connection with `connection_not_confirmed`.
open_points.question: Which refusal wins when the identifier is malformed, the connection record is invalid or outside its root, or the photo folder is unavailable?
options: Syntax, connection existence, confirmation, connection containment, then folder availability
Load and validate the connection before checking confirmation
Collapse invalid connections into `unknown_project`
open_points.default_guess: Apply syntax, existence, confirmation, containment and availability in that order.

open_points.subject: A5
open_points.text: A photo folder that resolves outside the root, or is missing, is refused with `folder_unavailable`.
open_points.question: How is containment preserved if a symlink or directory component changes after resolution but before or during scanning or placement?
options: Use descriptor-relative traversal with no-follow checks
Resolve once and trust the resulting path
Re-resolve before each file access
open_points.default_guess: Use descriptor-relative, no-follow traversal rooted at an already-open object directory.

open_points.subject: A5
open_points.text: A project id must be a UUID
open_points.question: Which UUID versions and textual forms are accepted, and is the canonical lowercase hyphenated form required?
options: Any RFC-valid UUID input, normalized canonically
Only lowercase canonical hyphenated UUIDs
Only the Registry's specific UUID version
open_points.default_guess: Accept the Registry's specified UUID version in canonical lowercase hyphenated form.

open_points.subject: A5
open_points.text: INV-09: a missing token, a wrong token and a token without the `Bearer` prefix are refused (`test_the_api_requires_the_token`).
open_points.question: What must show that every operation except health—not merely one tested endpoint—cannot succeed without authentication?
options: Parameterize the test over every operation and method
Narrow INV-09 to the tested API route
Use a routing-level authentication check plus a test enumerating the sole health exception
open_points.default_guess: Enumerate all routes and assert that only the health route bypasses the common authentication dependency.

open_points.subject: A5
open_points.text: INV-11: answers of scan and place contain neither the folder path nor the store path (`test_the_api_scans_and_places_without_showing_server_paths`), and the generated service has no Portal client or Portal credential setting.
open_points.question: What must show that mark answers and all error answers return no server path, and that the service never calls the Portal rather than merely lacking a named client or setting?
options: Inspect every answer schema and error path and enforce an import/network boundary
Narrow INV-11 to scan and place answers
Treat the listed checks as sufficient
open_points.default_guess: Add schema checks for all responses and a dependency/network boundary check proving no Portal call capability exists.

open_points.subject: A6
open_points.text: Records and images are replaced atomically, so a reader sees a complete file or none.
open_points.question: Is atomicity per individual file or across the image and its placement record, who the readers are, and why are immutable placement and mark records described as replaced?
options: Each individual filesystem object is installed atomically; image and record are not one atomic unit
Image and placement record become visible atomically as a pair
Only temporary-file replacement mechanics are required
open_points.default_guess: Specify per-file atomic replacement, with the placement record published only after the complete image is installed.

open_points.subject: A6
open_points.text: Placements and marks of one project run one at a time, across processes.
open_points.question: Do placement and marking share one project lock, where is that lock anchored, and what are its crash, timeout and stale-owner semantics?
options: One crash-safe interprocess lock per project shared by placement and marking
Separate placement and mark locks per project
Backend uniqueness constraints replace explicit locking
open_points.default_guess: Use one crash-released interprocess lock per project shared by placement and marking, with a specified bounded acquisition failure.

open_points.subject: A6
open_points.text: two concurrent placements and two concurrent marks with different `photo_id` values for one source leave one placement and one mark
open_points.question: Which caller succeeds, what exact result does each losing caller receive, and which `photo_id` becomes the mark?
options: First lock holder wins; the other placement replays and the other mark gets `publication_conflict`
Backend commit order wins
Either photo id may win and loser outcomes are unspecified
open_points.default_guess: The first completed write wins; the other placement returns `replayed` and the other mark returns `publication_conflict`.

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: Each operation reads it once.
open_points.question: Does “operation” include health checks, authentication failures, malformed requests, scans, replays and refusals, even when no current time is needed?
options: Every endpoint invocation reads exactly once
Only domain operations that compare or write a current instant read once
Only successful mutating operations read once
open_points.default_guess: Every domain operation that needs current time reads it exactly once; health, authentication failures and pure replays do not read it.

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: The current time is UTC without an offset.
open_points.question: What concrete representation, precision and rounding are required for clock values, comparisons and persisted `marked_at` values?
options: Naive UTC datetime with specified microsecond precision
Integer Unix time
RFC 3339 text without an offset
open_points.default_guess: Use a naive UTC datetime normalized to microsecond precision, with a specified serialization format.

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: A file's modification time is converted to the same form before it is compared or delivered.
open_points.question: Is filesystem modification time treated as an absolute POSIX instant or as local wall time, and what precision and rounding are used?
options: Convert the absolute filesystem timestamp to naive UTC
Interpret the displayed local filesystem time in Europe/Madrid
Round both clock and mtime to whole seconds
open_points.default_guess: Treat the filesystem timestamp as an absolute instant, convert it to naive UTC, and preserve the common supported precision.

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: INV-13: an operation given one fixed instant classifies every file against it and writes it as `marked_at` (`test_a_marked_photo_is_reported_as_published`, `test_a_file_still_arriving_is_not_placed`).
open_points.question: What must the Required test show to prove exactly one clock reading per operation, since fixed results do not distinguish one read from repeated reads returning the same instant?
options: Use a counting clock that fails or changes on a second read
Narrow INV-13 to consistent use of one supplied instant
Treat a fixed clock as sufficient evidence of one read
open_points.default_guess: Use a counting clock and assert exactly one read for each operation that needs time.

witness.initial: A clock returns the same fixed instant on every call.
events: An operation calls the clock once and produces the expected values.
Another implementation calls it once per file and produces the same values.
outcomes: The implementation violates INV-13 but passes both named tests.

open_points.subject: A8
open_points.text: The stored image limit must follow the Portal's deployment value if that value changes.
open_points.question: How can a fixed policy constant of 26,214,400 bytes follow a deployment-specific Portal value, and is a Portal change handled by configuration, a coordinated release or runtime discovery?
options: Make the limit a run setting coordinated with the Portal deployment
Keep a policy constant and require a coordinated code release
Read a shared deployment manifest
open_points.default_guess: Make it an explicitly named run setting validated against the Portal deployment configuration.

witness.initial: A Portal deployment raises or lowers its binary read limit.
events: The deliverer starts without a new build.
A prepared image is evaluated against the deliverer's limit.
outcomes: The deliverer follows the new deployment value automatically.
The deliverer continues using the compiled policy constant until released again.

open_points.subject: A8
open_points.text: Scan, placement and refusal statuses | as A1, A3, A4 and A5 | enumerations in the models
open_points.question: What are the exact enumeration types and complete member sets, including all refusal reasons, and which values belong to statuses versus reasons?
options: Define separate named enums for scan status, placement outcome and every refusal/reason family
Put every listed string in one enum
Leave endpoint-specific strings as unconstrained text
open_points.default_guess: Define separate named model enums with closed member lists and use their member names in notes.

open_points.subject: A9
open_points.text: The service runs only externally maintained libraries pinned to exact versions: the image library, the web framework, its data validation library and the web server.
open_points.question: Are transitive dependencies and other installed distributions allowed, must they also be exact-pinned, and which concrete packages and versions satisfy the decision?
options: Lock every direct and transitive distribution to exact versions
Exact-pin only the four named direct dependencies
Permit additional externally maintained libraries under the same review policy
open_points.default_guess: Maintain a complete lock of every direct and transitive distribution and explicitly name the four approved direct packages.

open_points.subject: A9
open_points.text: Before each deployment every installed distribution is checked against a current snapshot of the OSV database.
open_points.question: What makes an OSV snapshot current, which package identity and version matching rules apply, and does any matching advisory block deployment regardless of severity, withdrawal or applicability?
options: Define a maximum snapshot age and block every applicable non-withdrawn advisory
Query live OSV and block only advisories above a severity threshold
Block every raw match in the snapshot
open_points.default_guess: Require a successfully verified snapshot no older than a stated interval and block every applicable, non-withdrawn advisory unless a separately approved exception exists.

open_points.subject: A9
open_points.text: An image with a known vulnerability is not deployed, and a check that cannot complete does not pass.
open_points.question: What is the “image,” what action constitutes deployment, and which component enforces the refusal before that action?
options: The built service container image is gated before registry promotion or rollout
The prepared photo image is rejected
The host environment is audited during startup
open_points.default_guess: Treat “image” as the built service container and gate promotion or rollout in the deployment pipeline.

open_points.subject: A10
open_points.text: The total review of `SECURITY_REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md` over States 0 to 2. Each applicable category is owned by a decision above.
open_points.question: What authoritative category set makes the review total, and must every category—including non-applicable ones—appear explicitly in this section?
options: Use a named, versioned closed category list and require one outcome per member
Treat the displayed list as the complete set
Let the linter's current internal category list define completeness
open_points.default_guess: Name and version the closed category list and require an explicit applicable or not-applicable outcome for every member.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: Questions OQ-05, OQ-07 and OQ-08 stay open.
open_points.question: Which of these earlier open questions State 2 closes, which remain open, and where are the remaining questions deliberately carried, given that A2 and A5 cite OQ-05 and OQ-07 as normative rules?
options: A2 closes OQ-05 and A5 closes OQ-07; OQ-08 remains a Portal prerequisite
Only parts of OQ-05 and OQ-07 are closed and the residual questions remain open
All three remain open despite the cited rules
open_points.default_guess: Record the exact resolved and residual parts: A2 closes first-version section/caption behavior, A5 closes bearer authentication and HTTPS, while scan scope, deployment topology and OQ-08 remain explicit open prerequisites.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text: Syncthing's temporary files and the phone's trash are ignored.
open_points.question: Which A1 ignore rule implements the earlier promise about the phone's trash, since A1 names dot files, suffixes and unspecified Syncthing names but does not identify phone-trash names?
options: Phone-trash directories are included in the closed ignored-name set
All hidden directories are considered phone trash
The earlier claim is narrowed because phone-trash naming is not portable
open_points.default_guess: Add the exact phone-trash directory patterns to the closed ignored-name policy.

open_points.subject: A7
open_points.text: The service clock is the one source of the current time. Each operation reads it once.
open_points.rule: Иначе устроена `time_source_policy` (§6.8): её тоже проверяет гейт фабрики, но до кода она доходит через IR `system_clock_backend` (ниже, «Что считается достижимостью листа»), и декларация ей не нужна.
open_points.question: The passage must identify the time-source policy and its path through the `system_clock_backend` IR so generated code receives the decided clock rather than inventing one.

open_points.rule: | настройка запуска, зависящая от окружения | `config`, через модуль настроек (§6.11) | поле объекта настроек | поле модели настроек и его тип |

open_points.subject: A8
open_points.text: | Binary store root, state folder, connection record location | per installation | run setting |
open_points.rule: | настройка запуска, зависящая от окружения | `config`, через модуль настроек (§6.11) | поле объекта настроек | поле модели настроек и его тип |

open_points.subject: A8
open_points.text: | Source limit | 41 943 040 bytes | policy constant |
open_points.rule: | константа или таблица политики: пороги, имена, префиксы, закрытые наборы, таблицы правил | константа поставщика данных (§6.10) | `the imported X constant` | имя символа и его тип |
open_points.question: The passage must name the imported provider constant and its type.
